notes: Current USMLE reproductive/endocrine outline supports sex-steroid physiology.
Endotext and peer-reviewed aromatase-excess literature support CYP19A1 overexpression, increased aromatization, pre/peripubertal gynecomastia and advanced bone age.

exact_locator_notes: USMLE Content Outline — Reproductive and Endocrine Systems, sex-steroid physiology.
Endotext Gynecomastia — Etiology, increased aromatase activity/familial gynecomastia; aromatase excess syndrome review — CYP19A1 and clinical manifestations.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Familial prepubertal gynecomastia, advanced bone age and CYP19A1 overexpression identify aromatase excess; the direct biochemical effect is increased conversion of androgen substrates to estrogens.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: 5alpha-reductase and androgen-receptor defects reduce androgen effect, hepatic glucuronidation affects clearance, and activating LH-receptor signaling raises testosterone rather than directly explaining CYP19A1 gain of function.
